title: Interstate banking deregulation on credit supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Two-way fixed effects Difference-in-Differences (DID) and a single-cohort event study centered on period 4.
- Why: We compare branches in states that deregulate exactly at period 4 (treated=1) to branches in states that do not deregulate at period 4, before vs. after period 4. The outcome is log(loans/assets), so DID identifies the average treatment effect on the treated as a semi-elasticity.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of deregulation, trends in y for the period-4 deregulators and the comparison group would have evolved similarly. We probe this with an event study and a pre-period placebo.
  - No anticipation: No behavioral response prior to period 4 among treated.
  - SUTVA/stable composition: No spillovers across units and stable sample.
  - Given staggered adoption in the broader environment, we focus on the cohort that deregulates at period 4 and use all non-period-4 states as the comparison group; the event study is centered on period 4 for that cohort.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Packages
req_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest")
for (p in req_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
}
library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# 1) Read data
fpath <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s05_data.csv"
if (!file.exists(fpath)) stop(paste0("Data file not found at: ", fpath))
dt <- fread(fpath)

# Ensure proper types
dt[, unit_id := as.factor(unit_id)]
dt[, period := as.integer(period)]
dt[, treated := as.integer(treated)]
dt[, post := as.integer(post)]
dt[, treat_x_post := as.integer(treat_x_post)]
dt[, y := as.numeric(y)]

# Helper printer
print_did_result <- function(model, varname){
  b <- coef(model)[[varname]]
  se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(model)))[[varname]]
  ci_low <- b - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- b + 1.96 * se
  pct <- 100 * (exp(b) - 1)
  cat("Coefficient on", varname, "=", round(b, 4),
      "| SE =", round(se, 4),
      "| 95% CI [", round(ci_low, 4), ",", round(ci_high, 4), "]\n")
  cat("Implied percent change in loans/assets ≈", round(pct, 2), "%\n\n")
}

cat("=== Baseline DID (TWFE) ===\n")
# 2) Baseline DID with unit and time fixed effects; cluster at unit level
did <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)
print_did_result(did, "treat_x_post")

# 3) Event study around period 4 for the period-4 cohort
#    Implemented as interactions of time dummies with treated group,
#    omitting period 3 as the reference period.
for (p in sort(unique(dt$period))) {
  vname <- paste0("D", p)
  dt[, (vname) := as.integer(period == p & treated == 1L)]
}
# Omit D3 to make period 3 the baseline
es_formula <- as.formula(paste(
  "y ~", paste(setdiff(paste0("D", sort(unique(dt$period))), "D3"), collapse = " + "),
  "| unit_id + period"
))
est_es <- feols(es_formula, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)

cat("=== Event Study (relative to period 3 for treated cohort) ===\n")
# Print dynamic effects by relative time k = period - 3
all_p <- sort(unique(dt$period))
keep_vars <- setdiff(paste0("D", all_p), "D3")
coefs <- coef(est_es)[keep_vars]
ses <- sqrt(diag(vcov(est_es)))[keep_vars]
rel_k <- as.integer(gsub("D", "", keep_vars)) - 3
ord <- order(rel_k)
for (i in ord) {
  k <- rel_k[i]
  b <- coefs[i]; se <- ses[i]
  ci_l <- b - 1.96 * se; ci_h <- b + 1.96 * se
  cat("k =", sprintf("%+d", k),
      ": beta =", round(b, 4),
      "| SE =", round(se, 4),
      "| 95% CI [", round(ci_l, 4), ",", round(ci_h, 4), "]\n")
}
# Joint pre-trend test (k < 0 corresponds to periods 1 and 2, since 3 is baseline)
pre_vars <- paste0("D", all_p[all_p < 3])
if (length(pre_vars) > 0) {
  w_pre <- wald(est_es, paste(pre_vars, "= 0", collapse = ", "))
  cat("\nPre-trend joint test (coefficients on", paste(pre_vars, collapse = ", "),
      "):\n")
  print(w_pre)
  cat("\n")
}

# 4) Robustness checks
cat("=== Robustness: Two-way clustered SEs (unit and period) ===\n")
did_2c <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
print_did_result(did_2c, "treat_x_post")

cat("=== Robustness: Placebo DID in pre-periods only (t <= 3), fake policy at t=2 ===\n")
dt_pre <- dt[period <= 3]
dt_pre[, pseudo_post := as.integer(period >= 2)]
dt_pre[, placebo := treated * pseudo_post]
placebo <- feols(y ~ placebo | unit_id + period, data = dt_pre, cluster = ~ unit_id)
b_pl <- coef(placebo)[["placebo"]]
se_pl <- sqrt(diag(vcov(placebo)))[["placebo"]]
ci_l_pl <- b_pl - 1.96 * se_pl; ci_h_pl <- b_pl + 1.96 * se_pl
cat("Placebo coefficient =", round(b_pl, 4),
    "| SE =", round(se_pl, 4),
    "| 95% CI [", round(ci_l_pl, 4), ",", round(ci_h_pl, 4), "]\n\n")

cat("=== Robustness: Truncated window (periods <= 6) ===\n")
did_win <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt[period <= 6], cluster = ~ unit_id)
print_did_result(did_win, "treat_x_post")

# Final clean numeric output summary
cat("=== Summary (key number) ===\n")
b_main <- coef(did)[["treat_x_post"]]
se_main <- sqrt(diag(vcov(did)))[["treat_x_post"]]
ci_main <- c(b_main - 1.96 * se_main, b_main + 1.96 * se_main)
pct_main <- 100 * (exp(b_main) - 1)
cat("Main DID estimate (beta) =", round(b_main, 4),
    "| 95% CI [", round(ci_main[1], 4), ",", round(ci_main[2], 4), "]",
    "| Implied % change =", round(pct_main, 2), "%\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Interstate banking deregulation typically expands geographic diversification, lowers funding/monitoring costs, and intensifies competition, which tends to raise banks’ willingness to lend and the share of assets in loans.
- Magnitude: A modest but economically meaningful increase. In log terms, an ATT around 0.02–0.06 (≈2–6% higher loans-to-assets) is plausible for the period-4 cohort versus others, with dynamic effects showing a jump at k=+1 (first post period) and persistence thereafter, and statistically null pre-trends.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=deregulated states, control=still-regulated; shock=deregulation date
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit supply increases significantly after deregulation
